extracted.intended_audience: independent journalists, newsletter writers, and nonprofit newsroom audience/team leads
extracted.subtask_description: Best-practice guidance for independent journalists and nonprofit newsrooms on building and sustaining audiences for newsletters and digital reporting, including metrics, distribution, community engagement, and monetization strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research what your audience wants to know
rubrics_metrics.description: Use qualitative and quantitative research and analysis to understand readers' needs and interests and shape coverage accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The 19th tracks depth metrics and audience surveys to learn that readers gravitate toward reporting that explores policy in the context of people’s lived experiences (e.g., child care center closures, disability doulas). Use audience research to identify topics to commission and to reach underrepresented reader segments (e.g., researching issues that interest male readers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure depth over pageviews (track newsletter readers and Instagram engagements)
rubrics_metrics.description: De-emphasize pageviews as the primary growth metric and instead track metrics like newsletter readers, Instagram engagements, repeat visits, signups, and donations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 19th intentionally uses metrics like newsletter readers and Instagram engagements rather than time-on-site. Look for repeat platform visits, direct updates signups, and donations as signals of engagement and loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet readers where they are (distribute across platforms and partners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver reporting through the platforms and partner outlets your audience uses — e.g., email newsletters, Instagram, and republishing on partner platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 19th distributes via email, Instagram and republished articles with partners (PBS, Grist, Teen Vogue). Partnerships and republishing can extend reach; this is an alternative to forcing traffic to a single website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on organic social and search traffic rather than only paid marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize organic social distribution and search optimization as primary drivers of audience growth over paid marketing and advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 19th credited growth to organic social and search traffic plus partnerships rather than paid marketing. Prism relies heavily on Google searches as its largest traffic generator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track search queries to inform editorial strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor Google search terms and top reader questions to identify issues readers are curious about and to generate widely read reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prism tracks search terms (e.g., 'Should I join a union?' or 'Are you trans if you have PCOS?') and uses those questions as the basis for commissioning or writing articles. This centers the reader in editorial planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring the reader into the editorial room
rubrics_metrics.description: Use incoming questions and search trends to decide whether to report on topics or commission reporters, effectively inviting readers' concerns into editorial planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tracking shows a high volume of questions on a topic, ask 'Do we have reporting on this? Can we commission it if not?' — and involve readers through Q&A-style pieces or explanatory reporting based on their queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate trust through reporting and source relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience growth depends on trustworthy reporting; reporters must build relationships with sources and rapport with communities to maintain credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prism emphasizes that 'audience growth is coalition building' and that audience teams cannot succeed if trust is broken on the reporting side. Prioritize ethical sourcing and community rapport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a robust community engagement strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in sustained community engagement efforts to build relationships with the communities you cover, not just one-off outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 19th is developing community engagement strategies to build relationships with intended communities. Examples include community events, direct updates, and outreach that deepen ties beyond readership metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center storytelling on marginalized and misrepresented people when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape journalism and storytelling to reflect lived experiences of marginalized groups when that aligns with mission and audience needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 19th centers storytelling on marginalized and misrepresented people and focuses tightly on what those communities need and want, based on qualitative and quantitative research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment audience demographics to tailor coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Track reader demographics and use them to identify gaps and tailor coverage to reach underrepresented segments (age, gender identity, ideology, socioeconomic status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 19th found 60% of readers are women/nonbinary/trans; to reach more male readers they research topics likely to interest them. Tangle’s internal surveys revealed ideological and age breakdowns that informed outreach (e.g., starting a YouTube channel to reach younger readers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand coverage strategically to reach new constituencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Create or expand verticals and topic coverage (e.g., politics, policing, unionization, reproductive justice) to engage target audiences ahead of major events like elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prism is expanding coverage on politics and democracy to reach more readers going into the 2024 election, with separate verticals on hot-button issues to activate people toward civic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertise in related newsletters and leverage newsletter network effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Use advertising placements in other newsletters/platforms to reach receptive newsletter readers and benefit from newsletter readers' propensity to subscribe to other newsletters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tangle grew by advertising in other newsletters — 'newsletter readers are more likely to subscribe to other newsletters.' Newsletter advertising can be a high-value channel; Tangle’s advertising arm is much smaller than subscription revenue but aids discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert social followers into more permanent audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn ephemeral social media followings into durable audiences via owned channels (newsletters, communities) and direct engagement tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lyz Lenz converted Twitter followers to paying newsletter subscribers and created a Discord group; prescheduling posts and having a publishing calendar helps maintain continuity and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create community/network spaces (e.g., Discord) for engagement and peer collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Build community spaces for readers and for writers to network, share ideas, and recommend content — these spaces can boost engagement and cross-promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsletter writers used a Discord group to share story ideas, compare paywall rates, analyze traffic, and recommend each other’s articles — networking that supports audience growth and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a consistent publishing calendar and content cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a predictable schedule (e.g., an in-depth column weekly plus a lighter post midweek/weekend) to set reader expectations and sustain engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lenz publishes an in-depth column every Wednesday and a lighter post every Sunday; she preschedules posts or commissions guest writers before taking vacations to maintain cadence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversify platforms and formats to reach different age cohorts
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiment with other content formats and platforms (e.g., YouTube) to reach younger audiences who have different consumption habits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tangle started a YouTube channel to reach millennials and Gen Z because younger generations are more malleable in news habits and consume content on video streaming platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetize primarily through subscriptions rather than relying on advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize paid subscriptions as the main revenue driver to sustain staff and independent coverage; advertising can supplement but often yields less revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tangle’s 11,000 paying subscribers generate nearly $600,000 in annual revenue supporting staff, while advertising brings in roughly a tenth of subscription revenue—illustrating the stronger sustainability of subscriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't put all your eggs on a single social platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overreliance on any single social platform because platforms can decline or disappear; build owned channels and diversify distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lenz observed that 'Twitter is not going to be around forever' and emphasized converting followers to newsletters and other owned platforms to preserve audience reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the work enjoyable to keep the audience engaged
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain creative enjoyment and authenticity as part of editorial strategy—if the writer is bored, the audience will be bored too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lenz’s key lesson: 'It never hurts as a writer to create your own space and audience. If you’re bored, your audience is bored.' Prioritize sustainable, enjoyable work practices.
